source_refs.note: Exercise 13.1, Question 2 (book page 248, PDF 253); answer key PDF 310-311.

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) from first principles and find gradient of the curve at the given point: \(\sqrt{x + 2}\) at \(x = 6\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do kaam hain. Pehla: \(y = \sqrt{x + 2}\) ka \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) first principles se. Doosra: us formula mein \(x = 6\) rakh kar gradient (yani us point par tangent ki dhalaan / slope) nikalna.
Plan: square root hai, is liye chaar steps ke beech rationalising aayegi, bilkul Question 1(ii) ki tarah. Aakhir mein \(x = 6\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = f(x) = \sqrt{x + 2}\), point \(x = 6\).
Find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) aur \(x = 6\) par us ki value.
Tareeqa: definition (first principles / ab-initio, yani bilkul shuru se) se derivative: \(f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} \frac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\). Chaar steps yaad rakhein: (I) \(f(x + \delta x)\) likhein; (II) us mein se \(f(x)\) minus karein; (III) \(\delta x\) se divide karein; (IV) \(\delta x \to 0\) ka limit lein. Yeh tareeqa is liye ke Exercise 13.1 mein sawal khud 'by definition' maangta hai, aur power rule waghera abhi Section 13.6 mein aaenge; is liye shortcut nahi, poora limit ka safar dikhana hai. Curve ka gradient kisi point par \(f'\) ki us point par value hota hai, yani \(f'(6)\).

Step I aur II: farq nikalein
\[f(x + \delta x) = \sqrt{x + \delta x + 2}\]
\[f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = \sqrt{x + \delta x + 2} - \sqrt{x + 2}\]
Kyun: Root ke andar \(x\) ki jagah \(x + \delta x\) rakha; \(+2\) waisa hi rehta hai. Yahan \(\delta x\) root ke andar phansa hua hai, bahar nahi nikal sakta, is liye agla step rationalising hai.

Upar ko rationalise karein
\[= \dfrac{(x + \delta x + 2) - (x + 2)}{\sqrt{x + \delta x + 2} + \sqrt{x + 2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\delta x}{\sqrt{x + \delta x + 2} + \sqrt{x + 2}}\]
Kyun: Conjugate se upar neeche multiply kiya. Upar \(A^2 - B^2\) mein roots khatam ho kar \((x + \delta x + 2) - (x + 2) = \delta x\) bacha. Bracket lagana na bhoolein, warna \(-2\) ka sign ghalat ho jata hai.

Step III aur IV: divide karein aur limit lein
\[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x + \delta x + 2} + \sqrt{x + 2}}\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x + 2} + \sqrt{x + 2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 2}}\]
Kyun: \(\delta x\) cancel ho gaya. Phir \(\delta x = 0\) rakha; neeche \(2\sqrt{x + 2}\) bana jo zero nahi, is liye limit seedha mil gaya.

\(x = 6\) par gradient
\[f'(6) = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{6 + 2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{8}} = \dfrac{1}{2 \cdot 2\sqrt{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{8}\]
Kyun: Formula mein \(x = 6\) rakha. \(\sqrt{8} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 2} = 2\sqrt{2}\). Answer key \(\frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}\) likhti hai; \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{8}\) usi ka rationalised roop hai, dono sahi hain.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 6.01:\ \dfrac{\sqrt{8.01} - \sqrt{8}}{0.01} \approx 0.1767\]
\[\dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.1768 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(x = 6\) se thora sa aage ja kar average slope nikala to woh hamare jawab ke bohat qareeb aaya. Yehi derivative ka matlab hai: chhote se chhote interval par slope.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) from first principles and find gradient of the curve at the given point: \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x + a}}\) at \(x = a\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh Question 1(iii) jaisa hai, bas \(x\) ki jagah \(x + a\) hai. Yahan \(a\) ek constant (fixed number) hai, variable nahi; is ke saath number jaisa sulook karna hai.
Plan: do fractions ko ek banayenge, upar rationalise karenge, \(\delta x\) cancel, limit, aur aakhir mein \(x = a\) rakh kar gradient.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = f(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x + a}}\), \(a > 0\) constant, point \(x = a\).
Find karna hai: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) aur \(x = a\) par us ki value.
Tareeqa: definition (first principles / ab-initio, yani bilkul shuru se) se derivative: \(f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} \frac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\). Chaar steps yaad rakhein: (I) \(f(x + \delta x)\) likhein; (II) us mein se \(f(x)\) minus karein; (III) \(\delta x\) se divide karein; (IV) \(\delta x \to 0\) ka limit lein. Yeh tareeqa is liye ke Exercise 13.1 mein sawal khud 'by definition' maangta hai, aur power rule waghera abhi Section 13.6 mein aaenge; is liye shortcut nahi, poora limit ka safar dikhana hai.

Step I aur II: ek fraction
\[f(x + \delta x) - f(x)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x + \delta x + a}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x + a}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{x + a} - \sqrt{x + \delta x + a}}{\sqrt{x + a}\,\sqrt{x + \delta x + a}}\]
Kyun: Common denominator \(\sqrt{x + a}\,\sqrt{x + \delta x + a}\) le kar dono fractions ko ek kiya. Sirf \(x\) badalta hai; \(a\) constant hai is liye \(a\) ki jagah kuch nahi rakhte.

Upar ko rationalise karein
\[(\sqrt{x + a} - \sqrt{x + \delta x + a})(\sqrt{x + a} + \sqrt{x + \delta x + a})\]
\[= (x + a) - (x + \delta x + a) = -\delta x\]
Kyun: Conjugate se upar neeche multiply kiya. Upar roots khatam ho kar sirf \(-\delta x\) bacha. Neeche wala hissa factor form mein rehne dein; us mein conjugate bhi shamil ho gaya hai.

Step III aur IV: divide aur limit
\[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x} = \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{x + a}\sqrt{x + \delta x + a}\,(\sqrt{x + a} + \sqrt{x + \delta x + a})}\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-1}{(x + a) \cdot 2\sqrt{x + a}}\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{2(x + a)^{3/2}}\]
Kyun: \(\delta x\) cancel hua, phir \(\delta x = 0\) rakha. Neeche \(\sqrt{x + a}\cdot\sqrt{x + a} = x + a\) aur conjugate \(2\sqrt{x + a}\) bana. \((x + a)^{1} \cdot (x + a)^{1/2} = (x + a)^{3/2}\).

\(x = a\) par gradient
\[f'(a) = -\dfrac{1}{2(2a)^{3/2}}\]
\[(2a)^{3/2} = 2a\sqrt{2a} = 2\sqrt{2}\,a^{3/2}\]
\[f'(a) = -\dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}\,a^{3/2}}\]
Kyun: \(x = a\) rakha to \(x + a = 2a\) ban gaya. Phir \((2a)^{3/2} = 2a \cdot \sqrt{2}\sqrt{a} = 2\sqrt{2}\,a^{3/2}\). Is liye \(2 \cdot 2\sqrt{2} = 4\sqrt{2}\) neeche aata hai, jo answer key se milta hai.

Tasdeeq: Section 13.6 ke power rule se (sirf jawab confirm karne ke liye, tareeqa nahi)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x + a)^{-1/2} = -\tfrac{1}{2}(x + a)^{-3/2} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x + a}} = (x + a)^{-1/2}\); rule se bhi wohi general formula aata hai.
